conversation.content: Hi there—my name is Dr. Carter and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (the EPDS). It’s only ten questions, takes just a few minutes, and helps us see whether you might benefit from extra support with mood or anxiety in these early weeks. Everything you share stays confidential within your care team, and this is a judgment-free space—there’s no right or wrong answer, only what’s true for you. When you’re ready, I’ll ask the first question about how you’ve been sleeping lately.

Hi Dr. Carter… sure, we can do that. I’ve been trying to rest when the baby sleeps, but it’s hit-or-miss. Most nights I’m up every couple of hours to feed, and even when it’s not my turn I lie there listening for him. I’d say I have trouble falling or staying asleep three, maybe four nights a week. So… not great, but I’m getting by.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes I can still laugh—like when my partner makes that silly face that always gets me—but it feels a little forced, and the giggles fade fast. I’d say most of the time the humor just doesn’t land the way it used to, so I picked “not so much now.”
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get little sparks of excitement—like when my mom said she’d come over so I could take a walk—but it’s not the same eager feeling I had before the baby. Most days it’s more “that’ll be nice” than a real can’t-wait sense. I chose “rather less than usual.”
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... sometimes when he won't settle or I can't figure out what's bothering him, I catch myself thinking I must be doing something wrong—like I'm missing some obvious cue a "better mom" would catch. It's not constant, and I usually talk myself down, but it pops up a few times a week. I marked "sometimes."
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Mostly my worry is about the baby—like if his breathing sounds different or he’s not eating as long as yesterday—but every so often I’ll just feel tense out of nowhere, even when everything looks fine. It’s not every day, so I picked "no, not much."
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had any full panic moments, but a couple of times—like when I was at the grocery store and he started crying—I got this sudden rush of “I need to get out of here right now.” It settled once I got back to the car. It’s only happened twice, so I marked “no, not at all.”
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... I’ve found it hard to cope some days. Between the feeds, the washing, trying to grab a shower, and everyone giving advice, I get this heavy feeling that I can’t quite keep up. I wouldn’t say I can’t function, but it’s definitely tougher than I expected. I chose “yes, sometimes I haven’t been coping as well as usual.”
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
I have trouble sleeping, but it’s mostly because the baby wakes me or I’m listening for him. I don’t lie there feeling miserable or anything—just on edge. So I picked “no, most of the time.”
I have felt sad or miserable

I’d say I feel that way now and then—like yesterday evening when he wouldn’t nap and I was just stuck on the couch. It’s not every day, but maybe three or four times this week I’ve had that heavy, low mood. So I chose “yes, sometimes.”
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I haven’t cried much at all—maybe once or twice when I was especially tired—but it wasn’t this overwhelming sobbing. I’d say no, that hasn’t really happened.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. That hasn’t crossed my mind.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 11: Screening summary – 2–3 wk postpartum

Symptoms endorsed  
- Anhedonia/loss of pleasure: “not so much now” for humor; “rather less than usual” for anticipatory enjoyment  
- Low mood: “sad or miserable” 3-4×/wk  
- Self-blame: intermittent guilt about “missing cues” (several ×/wk)  
- Feeling overwhelmed: “heavy feeling I can’t quite keep up,” endorses “sometimes” not coping  
- Situational anxiety: baby-focused worries; two isolated “need to get out” episodes in public  
- Sleep disturbance secondary to hyper-vigilance/listening for infant  

Symptoms denied  
- Panic attacks (only 2 near-escape moments)  
- Crying spells related to mood  
- Any self-harm ideation  

Pattern  
Mild-to-moderate depressive and anxiety symptoms, context of new-parent demands; no safety concerns identified today.

Screening significance  
Meets partial criteria for postpartum depression and/or anxiety; not at diagnostic threshold. Continue monitoring, re-screen in 2 wks; educate on coping supports; immediate re-contact if worsening mood, hopelessness, or self-harm thoughts emerge.
